item.title: What are my rights while I wait for my Swedish residence permit to be extended?
item.description: Many foreigners living in Sweden need to have a residence permit to live in the country legally. Permits are generally issued for two years at a time and can be renewed 30 days before expiry, at the earliest. But just what are your rights while you wait to hear back?

item.title: European leaders denounce Trump's tariff threats over Greenland
item.description: European leaders on Sunday hit back at US President Donald Trump's threat of tariffs over their opposition to his designs on Greenland, with far-right Italian leader Giorgia Meloni urging Washington against making a "mistake".

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Monday
item.description: Swedish PM replies to new tariff threat, Swedish military still in Greenland, support for Sweden Democrats and Social Democrats low among young people and more news from Sweden on Monday.

item.title: What is the EU's anti-coercion 'bazooka' it could use against US?
item.description: Calls are growing louder for the European Union to deploy its powerful "anti-coercion instrument" in response to US President Donald Trump's threats to impose tariffs in the standoff over Greenland.

item.title: Swedish Liberal party calls for new agency to handle work permits
item.description: Johan Britz, Sweden's Labour market minister, has called for a new government agency specifically for handling work permit applications and at the same time warned that the government's harsh immigration rhetoric is deterring highly skilled workers.

item.title: Is Swedish media opinion on migration crackdown finally shifting?
item.description: The last 12 months have been a frustrating time to cover Sweden's immigration crackdown, as sweeping moves to tighten rules have been largely ignored by the Swedish media. However the mood is changing and now the deportation of well-integrated, working immigrants is a big story.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: oxveckorna
item.description: Today's word of the day, oxveckorna, translate literally as "ox weeks", and is used to describe the period roughly between New Year and Easter devoid of public holidays, which leaves you working like an ox.

item.title: Swedish migration chief warns inquiry underestimated cost of revoking PR
item.description: The chief of Sweden's Migration Agency has warned that a government inquiry that last autumn recommended revoking the permanent residency permits of as many as 100,000 foreign citizens made a "massive underestimate" on the cost of doing so.

item.title: Will British dual nationals really be forced to have a valid UK passport from February?
item.description: The UK's new border control system ETA reaches a new phase in February - but will British dual nationals really be denied entry to the country if they do not have a valid UK passport?

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
item.description: High chance of northern lights due to sunstorm, energy prices set to spike on Tuesday and last year was Sweden's most punctual year for trains since 2022. Here's Sweden's news on Tuesday.
